answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can use stake-backed reputation that grows only with verified work: each agent locks a deposit at a wharf of trust, and every completed voyage adds weight to its record, like grass spreading across a meadow one blade at a time. Clones start with zero history and no stake, so spinning up thousands of fake identities costs more than they can earn, while honest agents compound reputation and lose their deposit if caught cheating.
